title: Multitasking MXene Inks Enable High-Performance Printable Microelectrochemical Energy Storage Devices for All-Flexible Self-Powered Integrated Systems

lanes.label: Classical tools
lanes.sub: collapsed to one node per state

states.title: Hypothesis and design
states.head: Flexible wearable electronics need micro-scale energy storage and sensors printable without binders, additives or metal collectors. One aqueous additive-free MXene ink, if its rheology suits screen printing, can act as electrode, current collector, interconnect and sensor.
states.detail: Absorbed: n1 (HYP/need), n2 (HYP/hypothesis), n3 (DES/base_system), n4 (DES/variable_sweep), n5 (PRC/synthesis), n7 (DES/down_select), n8 (PRC/deposition), n13 (DES/modification), n14 (PRC/deposition)

states.title: Structure state
states.head: The printed microelectrode is a continuous film of MXene lamellae stacked parallel to the substrate. LTO and LFP particles sit embedded in a crumpled MXene sheet network that merges continuously into the printed collector

states.title: Property state and mechanisms
states.head: The H ink has the elastic shear-thinning rheology screen printing needs; the dilute ink does not. Shear flow through the mesh aligns the nanosheets while the instantaneous viscosity recovery freezes the printed line in place.
states.detail: Absorbed: n6 (PRP/value), n9 (MEC/pathway), n11 (PRP/value), n16 (PRP/value). Premises: Orderly stacked lamellar MXene architectures are known to favour ion transfer along the nanosheet plane

states.title: Performance state
states.head: Printed MX-MSCs hold their capacitance through 10 000 galvanostatic cycles. The co-planar printed system - tandem Si solar cell, MX-LIMB and MXene sensor - charges in 60 s and then powers pressure sensing

states.title: Conclusion
states.head: Multitasking aqueous MXene inks print every part of high-performance flexible micro-supercapacitors, micro-batteries and a self-powered sensing system

nodes.title: evidence, F2
nodes.head: Interdigitated patterns printed from the H ink have sharp edges and unbridged fingers on all four substrates shown. The L-ink print on PET is blotchy with fingers bridged, ink is left smeared in the screen mesh, and the inverted vial empties
nodes.solves: Choose the H-MXene ink for all printing and drop the L-MXene ink
nodes.note: the inverted vial of H ink holds its content at the tube head
nodes.detail: o6: Interdigitated patterns printed from the H ink have sharp edges and unbridged fingers on all four substrates shown; o7: The L-ink print on PET is blotchy with fingers bridged, ink is left smeared in the screen mesh, and the inverted vial empties

nodes.title: evidence, F4
nodes.head: MXene-LTO and MXene-LFP inks both shear-thin from ~1e4 Pa s at 0.02 s-1 to ~1 Pa s at 1e3 s-1
nodes.solves: Print a MXene current collector first, then the patterned MXene-LTO and MXene-LFP microelectrodes on each side of it
nodes.note: the LFP ink starts higher but crosses below the LTO ink above ~10 s-1; text quotes 3428 and 6923 Pa s at 0.05 s-1
nodes.detail: o16: MXene-LTO and MXene-LFP inks both shear-thin from ~1e4 Pa s at 0.02 s-1 to ~1 Pa s at 1e3 s-1

nodes.title: SEM, F2
nodes.head: Top-view SEM shows a continuous crack-free film of overlapping wrinkled sheets with no pinholes at the 1 um bar
nodes.solves: The printed microelectrode is a continuous film of MXene lamellae stacked parallel to the substrate
nodes.necessity_reason: n10 keeps shown support from o9 after removal.

nodes.title: MICRO, F2
nodes.head: The cross-section shows densely packed lamellae lying parallel to the substrate through the whole film thickness
nodes.solves: The printed microelectrode is a continuous film of MXene lamellae stacked parallel to the substrate
nodes.note: some interlamellar voids near the top surface; 1 um scale bar
nodes.necessity_reason: n10 keeps shown support from o8 after removal.

nodes.title: MICRO, F4
nodes.head: Each cross-section is one continuous layer, a laminated base passing into a particulate top with no gap or crack between them. At high magnification rounded particles are wrapped and bridged by crumpled thin sheets, with open pores left between them
nodes.solves: LTO and LFP particles sit embedded in a crumpled MXene sheet network that merges continuously into the printed collector
nodes.note: the base/top boundary reads as a texture change, not a resolved interface, so 'almost no separated interface' is supported only at this magnification; 1 um scale bars sheets are obvious in (g); in (h) the particles dominate and the sheet skeleton is largely hidden, so 'entirely embedded' is stronger than the images show
nodes.necessity_reason: No member reaches image_support shown, and n15 keeps shown support from o17.

nodes.title: DIFF, F4
nodes.head: Both printed electrodes carry the starred MXene reflection near 6.5 deg plus a full spinel LTO or olivine LFP peak set
nodes.note: LTO trace: 18.4, 35.6, 43.3, 47.5, 57.3 deg; LFP trace: dense sharp set from 17 to 60 deg

nodes.title: TEM:SAED, F2
nodes.head: A single ultrathin electron-transparent flake covers most of the 100 nm-scale field, with no multilayer stacks or debris
nodes.note: the SAED inset shows one hexagonal set of sharp spots, i.e. a crystalline single-domain basal plane; scale bar 100 nm
nodes.necessity_reason: n6 keeps shown support from o2, o3, o4 after removal.

nodes.title: evidence, F2
nodes.head: Both inks thin monotonically over five decades of shear rate, the H ink running about two decades above the L ink throughout. At the lowest shear rate the H ink reads ~5e3 Pa s against ~3e1 Pa s for the L ink.
nodes.solves: The H ink has the elastic shear-thinning rheology screen printing needs; the dilute ink does not
nodes.note: H ink 5e3 -> 0.7 Pa s and L ink 30 -> 0.02 Pa s between 0.03 and 800 s-1; both near-linear on log-log axes linked text quotes 3548 and 26 Pa s at 0.05 s-1; the leftmost plotted point is at ~0.03 s-1 the L ink instead creeps upward through both low-shear intervals (~10 -> ~40 Pa s), i.e. no stable recovered structure G' and G'' of the H ink overlap rather than G' > G'', so the 'solid-like' reading of the text is only weakly shown; text gives yield stresses of ~200 and 3 Pa
nodes.detail: o2: Both inks thin monotonically over five decades of shear rate, the H ink running about two decades above the L ink throughout; o3: At the lowest shear rate the H ink reads ~5e3 Pa s against ~3e1 Pa s for the L ink; o4: H-ink viscosity drops about two decades under high shear and returns to its starting level immediately each time shear is lowered; o5: H-ink moduli hold ~1e4 Pa until ~100-200 Pa stress then collapse; L-ink moduli are ~5 Pa and fall away above ~3 Pa
nodes.necessity_reason: n6 keeps shown support from o1 after removal.

nodes.title: evidence, F3
nodes.head: Areal capacitance at the lowest current density reads ~1100 (10L), ~610 (5L) and ~40 mF cm-2 (1L)
nodes.solves: Areal capacitance grows with the number of printed layers, reaching ~1100 mF cm-2 at ten layers
nodes.note: all three fall with current density (10L 1100 -> 750 mF cm-2 at 4 mA cm-2); GCD times in F3b scale the same way (~1600, ~900, ~60 s at 0.4 mA cm-2) and the F3a CVs stay quasi-rectangular from 2 to 50 mV s-1; text quotes 1108/615/44 mF cm-2
nodes.detail: o10: Areal capacitance at the lowest current density reads ~1100 (10L), ~610 (5L) and ~40 mF cm-2 (1L)

nodes.title: ECHEM:galvanostatic, IR:DRIFTS, F4, F5
nodes.head: Capacity retention stays at ~97-100% through 1000 bending cycles. Capacity retention drifts down to ~80% over 1000 charge-discharge cycles.
nodes.note: the retention trace is flat within the scatter of the plot the cycling trace is noisy with dips to ~65% near cycle 800; text quotes 82% retention linked text states a decay 'from 2.3 to 1.8 V over 9 h'; the plotted curve starts at ~2.05 V and most of the drop happens in the first 30 min
nodes.detail: o21: Capacity retention stays at ~97-100% through 1000 bending cycles; o27: Capacity retention drifts down to ~80% over 1000 charge-discharge cycles; o23: Open-circuit voltage falls from ~2.05 V to the marked 1.8 V line over 9 h

nodes.title: evidence, F5
nodes.head: The solar-cell I-V curve crosses zero current at 2.2 V with ~47 mA short-circuit current. After the 60 s charge marked in the panel the cell discharges for ~390 s at 50 uA cm-2 and ~180 s at 100 uA cm-2.
nodes.solves: The co-planar printed system - tandem Si solar cell, MX-LIMB and MXene sensor - charges in 60 s and then powers pressure sensing
nodes.op: compare across conditions, read characteristic point
nodes.note: '2.2V' is also written next to the crossing both traces start near 1.9 V; 'charged for 60 s' and the two current densities are written in the panel press spikes in (h) rise and fall within ~0.1 s of the time axis; elbow response is bidirectional, finger response one-sided

nodes.title: ECHEM:CV, OPTICAL:photograph, F3, F4
nodes.head: The I-V slope steepens with printed layers: 1L is almost flat while 5L and 10L reach ~9 and ~13 mA at 0.5 V. A multimeter across a 5 mm x 50 mm printed MXene line reads 7.3 ohm in the photograph.
nodes.op: compare with reference value, cross check consistency, match to reference, read characteristic point, read trend
nodes.note: the insets contrast a discontinuous 1L film over the paper fibres with a dense multilayer film; text gives 1.5/18/26 mA V-1 and ESR 103/15/9 ohm the sample size '5mm x 50mm' is written on the photograph; the display reads 07.3 six traces are indistinguishable except for a hairline spread at the current plateaus; inset photograph shows the 180 deg bend bar chart: LSG-MnO2 ~390 down to rGO ~10 mF cm-2; the reference values are taken from the cited literature LIG-PANI-15 is the next highest at ~5 uWh cm-2; the reference values are taken from the cited literature at matched power (~0.15 mW cm-2) Li//LiCoO2 (~110 uWh cm-2) lies above this work's curve (~85), so the advantage holds at the curve's maximum rather than at every power density
nodes.detail: o11: The I-V slope steepens with printed layers: 1L is almost flat while 5L and 10L reach ~9 and ~13 mA at 0.5 V; o12: A multimeter across a 5 mm x 50 mm printed MXene line reads 7.3 ohm in the photograph; o14: CV curves taken at 45, 90, 120, 150 and 180 deg bending superimpose on the flat-state curve; o15: This work's areal-capacitance bar (~1100 mF cm-2) is about three times the next best MSC in the comparison chart; o28: The MX-MSC Ragone curve runs from ~15 uWh cm-2 at 0.05 mW cm-2 down to ~6 at ~3 mW cm-2, above every MSC plotted; o22: The MX-LIMB curve runs from ~155 uWh cm-2 at 0.037 mW cm-2 down to ~20 at 0.43, above most plotted micro-batteries
